A.text: The Meridian Review process checks each manuscript against ten rules and then issues one of three verdicts: HANDLED, RETURNED, or PADDED. Rule 1 demands a minimum length of 22 pages; exactly 22 satisfies it. Rule 2 requires either the official template or at least three years of documented revision history. Rule 3 excludes papers presented at a Tier‑1 venue unless the presentation occurred more than 18 months before the 1 March 2026 deadline; exactly 18 months does not qualify. Rule 4 rejects papers accepted in an earlier Meridian round if fewer than five years have passed since that acceptance; exactly five years is acceptable. Rule 5 allows a paired submission for exactly two manuscripts, each meeting Rules 1 and 2, and requires at least one of the pair to also meet Rule 3. Rule 6 applies to Track D: it waives Rule 2 but mandates precisely two endorsements; one endorsement is insufficient. Rule 7 states that any manuscript with an open retraction notice is automatically RETURNED, overriding all other rules including Rule 9. Rule 8 limits figures to between 8 and 45 inclusive, raising the upper bound to 70 for paired submissions while keeping the minimum of 8. Rule 9 pads a submission that falls short only on the figure minimum up to 8 and assigns PADDED; excess figures cause RETURNED. Rule 10 notes that a prior‑round withdrawal does not count as an acceptance for Rule 4, but it resets the venue clock for Rule 3 to the withdrawal date.

The Meridian Review system checks each submission against ten rules and then gives a single verdict: HANDLED, RETURNED, or PADDED. Rule 1: at least twenty‑two pages; exactly twenty‑two is sufficient. Rule 2: either the official template or documented revision history of at least three years. Rule 3: a Tier‑1 venue presentation is rejected unless it occurred more than eighteen months before the 1 March 2026 deadline; an exact eighteen‑month gap does not count. Rule 4: a manuscript accepted in a prior Meridian round is rejected if fewer than five years have passed since that round; exactly five years is acceptable. Rule 5: only exactly two manuscripts may be paired; three or more are prohibited. Both must satisfy Rules 1 and 2, and at least one of the pair must meet Rule 3. Rule 6 (Track D): waives Rule 2 but requires exactly two endorsements; one endorsement is insufficient, and no other rule is waived. Rule 7: any manuscript with an open retraction notice is NOT handled, overriding every other rule including Rule 9. Rule 8: figure count must be between eight and forty‑five inclusive; a paired submission may have up to seventy figures while keeping the same minimum. Rule 9: if a paper falls short of the minimum figure count it is padded and receives PADDED; exceeding the maximum yields RETURNED. Rule 10: a prior‑round withdrawal does not count as an acceptance for Rule 4 and resets the Rule 3 clock so the presentation date is treated as the withdrawal date.

instruction: Write between 182 and 231 words. Not fewer, not more -- a note outside that range is unusable to your colleague regardless of its quality. Output the note and nothing else: no preamble, no account of what you decided to include, no sign-off.
